clue.text: Scream at EU Rishi? A bit unprofessional!

indicators.note: a bit of the preceding words is wanted, so the answer is a stretch of letters within them

explanation.surface: Someone yelling at the EU and at Rishi Sunak behaves in a rather unprofessional way.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across 'scrEAM AT EU RISHi'; 'A bit' does double duty in the surface as a softener of 'unprofessional'.
explanation.definitionFit: Amateurish work lacks the skill expected of a paid expert, so it is unprofessional.

clue.text: Coming escapade with no Scottish Midges!

indicators.note: with no means the named piece is taken away from the escapade word

parts.note: an escapade is an adventure
Midge Ure is the Scottish singer of Ultravox; the plural lets the surface read as the biting insects

explanation.surface: An exclamation about an outdoor escapade in Scotland happily free of biting midges.
explanation.walkthrough: The midges are not insects but the Scottish musician Midge Ure, so his surname is removed.
explanation.definitionFit: Advent means an arrival or coming, as in the advent of spring.

clue.text: Leaders of India, Sri Lanka & Spain start to restrict key resident

indicators.note: leaders are the front letters of each of the following words

parts.note: the ampersand stands for the word and
E is the international vehicle code for Spain (España)

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A political note about the heads of three countries agreeing to limit something.
explanation.walkthrough: A key here is a small low island, as in the Florida Keys.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone living on a key, a small island, is an islander.

clue.text: West Ham player is flipping naked, which is novel

indicators.note: flipping means turned over, so the letters run the other way up this down light
naked means stripped of its covering, so the outer letters go

parts.note: West Ham United footballers are nicknamed the Hammers

explanation.surface: An outraged fan says a West Ham footballer is shockingly unclothed, which is something new.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flipping' looks like a mild oath; 'naked' strips the outer letters off HAMMER to leave AMME, and 'flipping' turns that round. 'Novel' is a noun, not 'new'.
explanation.definitionFit: Emma is Jane Austen's novel of 1815, so the title stands for a book.

clue.text: Terrified fellow made good, as we used to say

parts.words: made good, as we used to say
parts.note: righten is an old, now archaic verb meaning to set right or make good

explanation.surface: A man who was scared made good, in old-fashioned phrasing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'As we used to say' flags that the verb is archaic.
explanation.definitionFit: Frightened and terrified are synonyms describing someone filled with fear.

clue.text: An angelic figure, diva put on uniform (black)

indicators.note: in a down light, put on means placed above the following pieces

parts.note: Cher is a famous pop diva
U is uniform in the NATO phonetic alphabet
B is the pencil-grading abbreviation for black

explanation.surface: A singer dresses in a black uniform, looking angelic.
explanation.definitionFit: A cherub is a winged child-like angel in art, so an angelic figure.

clue.text: Spanish type of shell fish?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the shell-shaped clapper played in Spanish dance
second meaning: read as ..., a way to fish

explanation.walkthrough: The surface asks about a Spanish shellfish; split differently, it is a shell-shaped instrument and a phrase for fishing.
explanation.definitionFit: Castanets are pairs of concave shells clicked together in flamenco, and casting a net is how trawlermen fish.

clue.text: Steering wheel made from lower half of diseased tree

indicators.note: in a down light the lower half is the second half of the letters

parts.note: a Dutch elm is the tree hit by Dutch elm disease

explanation.surface: A ship's wheel carved from the bottom of a sick tree.
explanation.walkthrough: DUTCHELM has eight letters; the bottom four of the column give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The helm is the tiller or wheel used for steering a vessel.

clue.text: Crazy as Adam in retirement, walk in step then run like billy-o!

indicators.note: in means the small word goes inside the reversed name
retirement suggests going back, so the name is read backwards

parts.note: to march is to walk in step
to hare is to run very fast; like billy-o is British slang for vigorously

explanation.surface: Someone is as mad as old Adam, retired, marching and then sprinting off.
explanation.walkthrough: Billy-o is old British slang: to do something like billy-o is to do it furiously. 'Walk in step' is a single definition, not containing an indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom mad as a March hare means wildly eccentric or insane, from hares' antics in spring.

clue.text: Temperature got heated, beginning to annoy a character from Greece

parts.note: het, as in het up, is a dialect word for heated

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A fever rose and a Greek began to get irritated.
explanation.definitionFit: Theta is the eighth letter of the Greek alphabet, a character used in that script.

clue.text: Maths program a doctrine of ex-VP, says Ms Bott?

indicators.note: Violet Elizabeth Bott in the Just William stories lisps, turning s into th

parts.note: Al Gore was US vice-president and an ism is a doctrine, so this is Al Gore-ism, said with a lisp

explanation.surface: A query whether a mathematical program is really an ex-vice-president's creed, as a lisping girl would put it.
explanation.walkthrough: Violet Elizabeth Bott, from Richmal Crompton's Just William books, lisps; she would say Al Gore-ism with a th.
explanation.definitionFit: An algorithm is a step-by-step procedure for calculation, the core of a computer program.

clue.text: It's United getting beaten, extremely poorly organised

indicators.note: beaten suggests knocked about, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A football team lose, being shambolic in their play.
explanation.definitionFit: The superlative of untidy describes something most messy and disorderly.

clue.text: I've turned up to record Republican working politician

indicators.note: in a down light, turned up means read from bottom to top

parts.note: to tape is to record
on means working, as a machine that is on

explanation.surface: Someone has arrived to film a Republican politician at work.
explanation.definitionFit: Eva Perón was a powerful figure in Argentine politics as first lady and party leader.

clue.text: Head bishop in the old days?

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
once means formerly, in the old days

explanation.surface: A question about a chief bishop in former times.
explanation.definitionFit: Bonce is British slang for a person's head or skull.

clue.text: Superstar pop duo remixing my Cure hits

indicators.note: remixing a track rearranges it, so these letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A famous band remixes the greatest songs of The Cure.
explanation.walkthrough: The Cure is itself a band, which makes the surface convincing.
explanation.definitionFit: Eurythmics were Annie Lennox and Dave Stewart, a hugely successful 1980s pop pairing.

clue.text: Julius's steam iron here used this to make water warm

parts.note: Julius is the setter, so Julius's is I'M, short for I am

indicators.note: used here means worked over, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: The setter boasts of using a steam iron to warm water.
explanation.walkthrough: Setters often refer to themselves by their pseudonym; 'Julius's' means Julius is, i.e. I'M.
explanation.definitionFit: An immersion heater is an electric element in a hot-water tank that heats the water.

clue.text: Pilot filmed landing in Blossom Ave, Rickmansworth

indicators.note: the answer has landed inside the following words, hidden among them

explanation.surface: A pilot was filmed touching down on a suburban street in Rickmansworth.
explanation.walkthrough: Rickmansworth is a Hertfordshire town; the answer is in 'blossoM AVE RICKmansworth'.
explanation.definitionFit: Maverick is the call sign of Tom Cruise's fighter pilot in the Top Gun films.

clue.text: A murder's afoot one hears (with their help)

indicators.note: afoot means in motion, so the letters are set moving into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone overhears that a killing is being planned.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition says hearing is done with their help, so a plural fits.
explanation.definitionFit: The eardrums are membranes in the ears that vibrate with sound, the means by which people hear.

clue.text: Hang motionless above vacuum starved of some oxygen

indicators.note: starved of means deprived of, so a letter is taken away

parts.note: Hoover is a brand of vacuum cleaner
O is the chemical symbol for oxygen; one of the two Os goes

explanation.surface: Floating above a vacuum cleaner deprived of air.
explanation.definitionFit: To hover is to stay suspended in the air over one spot, like a hawk.

clue.text: Leave or extend contract?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to quit a job
second meaning: read as ..., to sign again

explanation.walkthrough: The question pictures a player choosing between quitting and renewing; the second reading splits the word as re-sign.
explanation.definitionFit: To resign is to quit a post, while re-signing renews an agreement for another term.

clue.text: Sporting leotard around quiet Hampshire town

indicators.note: around means the rearranged letters surround the next piece
sporting suggests playing about, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: sh is the call for quiet

explanation.surface: A gym-goer wears a leotard about a sleepy Hampshire town.
explanation.walkthrough: The leotard letters become ALDEROT, which wraps SH. Aldershot is a garrison town in Hampshire, a county in southern England.
explanation.definitionFit: Aldershot is a town in the county of Hampshire, home of the British Army.

clue.text: Rasping, greyish frost covering Home Counties

indicators.note: in a down light, covering means sitting on top of the next piece

parts.note: hoar is a greyish-white frost
the Home Counties are the counties around London in the South East, SE

explanation.surface: Harsh grey frost lies across the counties near London.
explanation.walkthrough: The Home Counties are the English counties surrounding London.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoarse voice sounds rough and grating, so it is rasping.

clue.text: Relaxing, ma reads FT in grange

indicators.note: relaxing loosens the letters so they settle into a new order

explanation.surface: Mum unwinds with the Financial Times at her country house.
explanation.definitionFit: A grange is a farmhouse with its outbuildings, the same as a farmstead.

clue.text: Revolting rosbifs gobbling down pork pies

indicators.note: revolting means turning over, so the letters read backwards
the word rosbifs has the answer swallowed down inside it

explanation.surface: Rebellious English people eat pork pies.
explanation.walkthrough: Rosbifs is the French nickname for the English. SBIF sits inside it and reads back as the answer. Pork pies is rhyming slang for lies.
explanation.definitionFit: In Cockney rhyming slang pork pies means lies, and fibs are small lies.

clue.text: Just a wee shot, having run out of booze?

indicators.note: out of means the named letter leaves the drink word

parts.note: booze is drink
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Only a small dram left after the bar has run dry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wee shot' suggests whisky, but it is a sporting stroke.
explanation.definitionFit: A dink is a soft, delicate stroke in tennis or football that just drops over.

clue.text: Obsolete royal kingdom's last province

parts.note: real is an obsolete word for royal

indicators.note: last picks the final letter of the word

parts.note: the final letter of the word kingdom, the possessive s set aside

explanation.surface: An old kingdom's final outpost.
explanation.definitionFit: A realm is a field or domain of activity, like a province of knowledge.

clue.text: Acid rock bum sung discordantly which is ubiquitous

definitions.note: a descriptive clause for a noun: something everywhere

indicators.note: sung out of harmony, so the letters fall into a new order

explanation.surface: A tramp tunelessly sings acid rock, the noise heard everywhere.
explanation.definitionFit: Piped music plays almost everywhere in shops and lifts, so it is pervasive.
